workarounds.symptom: update: a version npm announces but does not serve yet fails the update

Target files: implementations/cli/smoke/command-kernel.smoke.ts, implementations/cli/src/commands/update.ts, packages/workspace/src/updates.ts. In the minutes after a release, npm names the new version as latest before every registry read serves it. `cotal update --self` then picked the version, `npm install` answered `ETARGET`, and the update was reported as failed and rolled back. Target files: lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/weaviate_tool/vector_search.py, lib/crewai-tools/tests/tools/test_weaviate_tool.py. `WeaviateVectorSearchTool` declares a `headers` field and passes it to `weaviate.connect_to_weaviate_cloud()`, but `__init__` always replaced it with `{"X-OpenAI-Api-Key": <env>}` and raised when `OPENAI_API_KEY` was unset — even when the caller had supplied the header. Callers using a custom vectorizer or generative model could not auth... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9348)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] crewai install exits 0 when uv sync fails
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(cli): exit with the uv status when crewai install fails. Target files: lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/cli.py, lib/cli/tests/test_install_command.py. `crewai install` printed a failed `uv sync` and exited `0`. `install_crew()` only re-raises when the caller opts in with `raise_on_error=True`, and the CLI command used the default, unlike the `deploy` and `run` paths which already translate the failure into `SystemExit(e.returncode)`. CI jobs and install scripts therefore saw a successful install after a dependency resolution fail... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9346)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] crewai deploy and crewai tool publish can't read a non-ASCII pyproject.toml on Windows
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(core): read pyproject.toml as utf-8 in project helpers. Target files: lib/crewai-core/src/crewai_core/project.py, lib/crewai-core/tests/test_project.py. `_get_project_attribute()`, behind `get_project_name()`, `get_project_version()` and `get_project_description()`, opened `pyproject.toml` without an encoding. On Windows the file was decoded with the ANSI code page (cp1252) instead of UTF-8. A `pyproject.toml` with CJK text, or a letter such as "č" or "Ł", made `crewai deploy` and `crewai tool publish` stop with "Unable... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9414)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] @CrewBase fails with unhashable type: 'dict' when an agent's llm in agents.yaml is a mapping
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(project): accept an llm mapping in agents.yaml. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/project/crew_base.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_project.py. `@CrewBase` checked every `llm` and `function_calling_llm` value in `agents.yaml` against the crew's `@llm` methods with `llms.get(value)`. A mapping of LLM settings (`model`, `temperature`, ...), which `Agent` itself accepts through `create_llm()`, is a `dict` and can't be used as a key. So the crew failed with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` before any agent was built. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9421)
